messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Alice Novak <alice@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: (Action) Aggregated route rollup: workshop + requirements

Team —

Quick summary: ACME flagged that their observability needs are fractured across per-route tiles; they asked if we can ship a consolidated "rollup" view that groups related endpoints, shows cost/latency aggregates, and surfaces top offending token paths. They want this for their upcoming Q3 reliability review (deadline: 2027-08-12).

Why this matters: shipping a coherent aggregation surface will reduce customer confusion, lower our support load (fewer tickets asking "which endpoint is burning tokens?"), and unlock a per-account SLA rollup we can eventually charge for.

Proposed next steps: 
- Run a 60-minute cross-functional workshop to align scope (data model, UX, rollups vs. slices).
- Share a lightweight requirements doc + mockup before the workshop.
- Output: rough implementation plan and an owner for a small spike to validate aggregation performance.

I've attached a quick mockup and a first-pass requirements draft (rollup-requirements-v1.md). Can everyone confirm availability for a 60-min sync next week? My suggested slots: Tue 6/29 10–11am PT or Wed 6/30 2–3pm PT.

Specific asks: 
- Marissa: can you bring the telemetry constraints (sample rates, retention windows) so we know what aggregates are feasible?
- Aditya: can you outline expected query cost implications if we precompute rollups daily vs on-demand?
- Jasmine: can you sketch the quick UX options (single-pane vs tabbed) and which one fits our Console chrome?

ACME (Alice) is ok attending the workshop if we want customer context; leaving them cc'd.

Thanks,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Console 
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-27T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (Action) Aggregated route rollup: workshop + requirements

Kim —

Thanks for kicking this off. Happy to join the workshop. Quick notes from telemetry side: 
- We currently sample full traces for ~5% of requests in prod (configurable per-tenant). That limits some per-route tail analysis unless we increase sampling or enable targeted sampling for named rollups.
- Precomputed daily rollups look cheap if we aggregate counters and token totals; the expensive part is per-path token replay (that requires stored mini-traces).

I'll bring cost estimates and a diagram of the sampling tradeoffs. Tue 6/29 10am PT works for me.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Observability 
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Alice Novak <alice@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (Action) Aggregated route rollup: workshop + requirements

Kim / all —

Heads-up on implementation constraints from the serving/runtime side: 
- Aggregations of token counts and p50/p95 latency per-route are straightforward via nightly MapReduce over our usage hive. Incremental windows (hourly) are also feasible but increase compute.
- If we want per-token-path top offenders ("top token sinks"), we need to persist condensed path summaries (KV sketches) at request time; that adds ~2–5% CPU and 30–80MB/day per high-traffic tenant if we keep 7 days of windowed sketches.
- Important fallback: we can build an initial MVP that exposes aggregated metrics and a lightweight "sample playback" that only works for sampled sessions (no full path reconstruction). That reduces cost and gets value quickly.

I'll prepare a short slide with two implementation tiers (MVP: aggregated counters + sampled playback; Tier 2: persistent path sketches + ranked offenders).

Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — workshop confirmed Tue 6/29 10–11am PT (calendar invite sent). Agenda I'll run: 
1) Goal & success criteria (Kim) — what signals indicate this shipped feature helps customers?
2) Data model & telemetry constraints (Marissa) — what we can compute reliably today
3) UX directions (me) — single-pane rollup vs nested route list; mockups review (see attached PNG)
4) Implementation tiers & perf/cost tradeoffs (Aditya)
5) ACME context & ask (Alice) — what they need for their Q3 review
6) Owners & immediate next steps (action items)

Action before workshop: Kim please update rollup-requirements-v1.md with ACME's top-3 views they want (they mentioned "Total token spend by logical product area", "Top expensive flows", "SLA exposure by account"). I've added these to the shared doc link.

I'll also bring two mockups: a compact table with inline sparkline (low-space) and a multi-column card view (richer detail). From a Console chrome perspective the compact table maps better to existing pages and will be faster to iterate on.

See you all tomorrow.

Jasmine

--
